label: The computer is a container of its own, not a mode of the server: entrypoint /app/bin/openbot-computer, so a bot's shell reads only what that service is given, with no database address, keys or licence.
The computer is loopback-only because it drives a browser holding real logins, and COMPUTER_TOKEN is the request control.
The browser is headed by default on the container's own X server because bot checks such as Cloudflare's challenge treat headless worse; headless is opt-in.
Browser capacity is bounded by count, idle time and memory: 8 browsers, 30 minutes idle, and closing at 85 percent of container memory down to ten points under.
Files persist on two volumes, agent-workspace:/workspace and agent-profiles:/profiles, the second so logins survive container restarts.
A shared computer still separates bots: COMPUTER_SEPARATE_WORKSPACES gives every bot without a computer of its own its own folder of files, and its shell starts there.
The supervisor is the only holder of the Docker socket, which is root-equivalent on the host, and it exposes only bot-level verbs.
Each per-bot computer is created from the same image with its own token derived from the deployment token and whose computer it is, so a bot that reads its own token opens no other.
gVisor is opt-in, not default: COMPUTER_RUNTIME=runsc runs every computer under gVisor when the host has it, and unset means an ordinary container sharing the host kernel.
Egress is per bot: EGRESS_PROXY_<BOT> is derived from the bot's id, so there is no fixed list to write out.

Start cost is real and budgeted: a sleeping or new computer costs a node, a pod and a browser launch, over a minute and a half on a busy day, so the server waits 180 seconds rather than reporting a failed step.
